q1.title: How large is announced demand beside a recent system margin?
q1.verdict: The figures are comparable in scale, but the national margin is not site connection headroom.
q1.stat: 1,500 MW forecast by 2028 vs a 3,629 MW May 2026 system margin
q1.blurb: DICT's 2028 forecast alone equals 41% of the whole system's May margin, and Meralco has committed 1,000 MW for 10 data centers. A data center is near-flat 24/7 load. IEMOP dispatch schedules recorded load curtailed on 130 grid days in this archive window (9,066.8 MWh). These figures establish scale; they do not establish connection headroom for a particular project.
q1.src: IEMOP May 2026 report; PCIJ (Meralco commitment); DICT forecast via BusinessWorld; IEMOP RTD regional summaries

q2.title: What do public records say about connection capacity?
q2.verdict: They show where equipment reached a limit, but they do not publish available capacity for a specific site.
q2.stat: 86 distinct pieces of equipment (103 monitored constraints) hit limits across the real-time and day-ahead runs on 135 archive days; the Leyte-Luzon HVDC ran at max or offline 69% of Dec 2025
q2.blurb: The inter-island links and named 230 kV lines already reach their limits often; the table names the affected equipment. Nearly every announced data-center megawatt sits on Luzon, which already supplies power south over those links. Connection capacity still has to be checked at the actual site and interval. Luzon scheduled reserves fell below the stated requirement in at least one 5-minute interval on 76 of the window's days.
q2.src: IEMOP congestions-manifesting files; IEMOP Dec 2025 report; IEMOP outage schedules

q3.title: How do recorded prices differ by grid?
q3.verdict: Regional prices separate by day and interval. Retail bills reflect the monthly purchase mix, not one spot interval.
q3.stat: May 2026: ₱7.79/kWh system (+38.5% vs April); Luzon ₱7.02, Visayas ₱10.2, Mindanao ₱9.28
q3.blurb: Regional prices can separate when an inter-grid link reaches its limit. While WESM ran administered prices (through 2026-05-01), the three grids stayed within ₱0.015/kWh of each other; once trading resumed the mean daily high-to-low spread across the three grids was ₱5.29/kWh. Widest daily regional spread in the archive: ₱15.722/kWh on 2026-06-08. WESM passes into the Meralco generation charge monthly, and only on the share of energy actually bought on the spot market: June paid ₱7.0281/kWh for the 10% it drew from WESM, about ₱0.70/kWh of the ₱9.0704/kWh generation charge. The rest is contracted and does not move with the spot price. New flat 24/7 load raises the demand the market clears against in every interval.
q3.src: IEMOP monthly reports; archived LWAP files; Meralco June 2026 advisory
